target.title: fix(agents): decouple MCP retirement from browser cleanup
target.body:
Related: #76233
Related: #101830

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a completed run-mode subagent waits for sequential browser-tab cleanup before retiring its bundle MCP runtime and starting completion delivery. A browser close request can wait up to the browser service timeout per tab, so one run with several tabs can delay MCP retirement, the completion announcement, and the next same-session turn.

The concrete sequential browser-cleanup delay is separate from the MCP lease-disposal race covered by #76233 and the related #101830 work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Browser cleanup is dispatched as independent owner-scoped work, while MCP retirement and completion announcement proceed after the existing generation and lease-safety checks. Browser operations hold a per-session access gate for their full request; cleanup takes the exclusive gate, so a successor browser turn waits safely instead of racing an already-issued close request.

The browser registry tracks the opaque run owner and an ordered ownership claim. Successor reuse transfers ownership; late predecessor callbacks cannot reclaim or remove the successor tab. Failed non-ignorable closes remain tracked for a later cleanup, and legacy unowned tabs remain eligible for cleanup.

`runId` remains an additive, optional Plugin SDK context field. It is host-issued, stable for the active run, opaque, and absent outside an active run. Plugins may use it only to key ephemeral plugin-owned resources and cleanup; they must not parse it, persist it as application data, expose it to users, or use it as an authentication or authorization boundary. The contract is documented in `docs/plugins/building-plugins.md` and covered at the `defineToolPlugin` factory boundary in `src/plugin-sdk/tool-plugin.test.ts`; the existing agent-context test covers runtime propagation.

## User Impact

Run-mode subagent completion no longer waits for the browser service to close every tracked tab before MCP retirement and completion delivery begin. A successor turn can start its non-browser work immediately and its browser work is admitted after the old cleanup gate releases, preserving tab safety. App-view MCP leases continue to defer retirement until their release path completes.

target.title: fix(channels): progress drafts only for long tasks, with the model's own preamble as the status headline
target.body:
Closes #105872

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes progress drafts appearing for small tasks even though the draft gate nominally waits five seconds. The second work event bypassed that delay, and the utility narrator could spend a model call before any draft was visible. Progress-mode channels also discarded the model's typed preamble even though it is the most accurate status headline available.

## Why This Change Was Made

The draft gate is now purely time-based; explicit immediate paths such as approvals and patches remain immediate. Utility narration starts only after the draft becomes visible. The shared compositor prefers fresh, typed model preambles as the headline, then uses utility narration only when the preamble is absent or stale. No config or model-facing tool surface was added.

The implementation preserves preamble item identity and retractions, counts only sanitized commentary that the compositor accepts, cancels narrator retries and expiry timers when a turn settles, rejects stale in-flight utility results, resets queued-turn lifecycle state, and refreshes same-text headlines when a new preamble item arrives.

## User Impact

- Fast turns produce only the final answer: no transient draft, receipt, or utility narration call.
- Long turns show the model's current preamble as the status headline, with utility narration filling genuine silences and tool activity retained below it.
- Retractions clear the matching headline, final delivery removes the draft, and queued turns begin with fresh lifecycle state.

target.title: fix(restart-sentinel): log DB errors instead of silently swallowing them
target.body:
## Summary

`clearRestartSentinel`, `readRestartSentinel`, and `hasRestartSentinel` used empty `catch {}` / `catch { return null }` / `catch { return false }` blocks that silently swallowed SQLite DB errors. This PR replaces them with `sentinelLog.warn(...)` so errors are visible in diagnostics while preserving the best-effort semantics.

## What Problem This Solves

In `src/infra/restart-sentinel.ts`, three exported functions silently discard all errors from the SQLite state database:

- **`clearRestartSentinel`** — `catch {}`: If the DB write fails (locked, corrupt, disk full), the sentinel is not cleared but the caller has no way to detect this. The gateway may continue to believe a restart is pending.
- **`readRestartSentinel`** — `catch { return null }`: Any DB read error (transient lock, corruption) is treated identically to "no sentinel exists", potentially causing a pending restart to be silently dropped.
- **`hasRestartSentinel`** — `catch { return false }`: Same problem — DB errors are indistinguishable from "no sentinel".

**Code evidence**: In `restart-sentinel.ts:228`, the `catch {}` on the `runOpenClawStateWriteTransaction` call provides no visibility into whether the sentinel was actually cleared.

## Root Cause

The functions were written with best-effort semantics (they must not throw during shutdown/cleanup), but the empty catch blocks went too far by discarding all diagnostic information. Unlike the intentional best-effort pattern in `ensureOpenClawStatePermissions` (which includes a comment explaining why the catch is empty), these catch blocks had no explanation and no logging.

## Why This Fix

Follows the same pattern accepted in:
- [#84449](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/84449) (`fix(delivery): log failDelivery errors instead of silently swallowing`) by @SebTardif
- [#82943](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82943) (`fix(agents): log warnings instead of swallowing subagent errors`) by @SebTardif

Uses `createSubsystemLogger("restart-sentinel")` + `formatErrorMessage(err)` — consistent with `restart.ts` which also uses `createSubsystemLogger("restart")`.

## User Impact

- **Before**: Operators had no diagnostic signal when the restart sentinel could not be cleared or read — failures were completely invisible.
- **After**: A warning is emitted to the diagnostics log (`[restart-sentinel]` prefix) with the full error context, while the functions continue to return safe defaults (`null` / `false` / `undefined`).

## Evidence

- **Before**: No warnings emitted on stderr when the DB operation fails — errors are silently swallowed.
- **After**: Three warnings emitted with full error context; functions return safely without throwing.

## Real Behavior Proof

### Before (on main, `catch {}`)
```bash
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-restart-sentinel-catch.mjs
=== clearRestartSentinel ===
clearRestartSentinel completed without throwing

=== readRestartSentinel ===
readRestartSentinel returned: null

=== hasRestartSentinel ===
hasRestartSentinel returned: false

=== stderr (warnings captured) ===
FAIL: No warnings were emitted on stderr!
      The catch blocks are silently swallowing errors.
```

### After (with fix)
```bash
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-restart-sentinel-catch.mjs
=== clearRestartSentinel ===
clearRestartSentinel completed without throwing

=== readRestartSentinel ===
readRestartSentinel returned: null

=== hasRestartSentinel ===
hasRestartSentinel returned: false

=== stderr (warnings captured) ===
PASS: Warnings were emitted on stderr:
  [restart-sentinel] Failed to clear restart sentinel: ...
  [restart-sentinel] Failed to read restart sentinel: ...
  [restart-sentinel] Failed to check restart sentinel: ...
```

## Tests and Validation

- `pnpm check` passed (no lint errors)
- Added 3 regression tests in `restart-sentinel.test.ts` verifying that each function survives DB failures without throwing and returns the safe default value

target.title: feat(exec): deny-over-allow exec approval denylist (#6615)
target.body:
Fixes #6615. Supersedes #92456 (author inactive since 2026-06-12, no response to review, conflicts with main — full credit to @Hidetsugu55 for the STOP-list concept and dual-host enforcement approach, both kept here).

## Update — re-review 2 (clawsweeper P1 blockers resolved)

The previous review's three P1 blockers were "contract declared but not wired." All three are now wired end-to-end, with focused tests on each exact path plus refreshed real-behavior proof. Also merged latest `origin/main` (resolves the CONFLICTING/behind-main note).

- **[P1] Wire `tools.exec.denylist` into config schema + gateway caller** — `denylist` added to the strict zod `ToolExecBaseShape` (`src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts`, non-empty-pattern refinement) so `openclaw config validate` accepts it and rejects malformed entries; threaded as `execConfigDenylist` through `agent-tools.ts` → `bash-tools.exec.ts` → `processGatewayAllowlist`, unioned across global + per-agent layers (`resolveEffectiveExecDenylist`). Tests: `config.schema-regressions.test.ts`, `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts`.
- **[P1] Pass denylist hits into node-host `system.run`** — `invoke-system-run.ts` now evaluates the effective denylist (openclaw.json global + per-agent + `exec-approvals.json` file layer) and passes `denylisted`/`denylistReason` into `evaluateSystemRunPolicy`; the model auto-reviewer is hard-blocked on a hit (human-only), and unanalyzable commands fail closed. Tests: `invoke-system-run.test.ts` (+ node denial reason `denylist-hit`).
- **[P1] Add denylist to exec-approval protocol writes** — `ExecApprovalsDenylistEntrySchema` + `denylist` added to `ExecApprovalsPolicyFields` in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/exec-approvals.ts` so `exec.approvals.set` / `exec.approvals.node.set` round-trip the field. Tests: `exec-approvals-validators.test.ts`.

Two extra hardening changes made while wiring the above:

- **Real defect fix:** `sanitizeExecApprovalPolicy` (`src/infra/exec-approvals.ts`) was silently dropping the defaults-layer `denylist` on every `saveExecApprovals` write — a routine policy write would disarm an operator's STOP list. Now normalized and preserved.
- **Standalone gate:** the gateway host now has an independent `requiresDenylistApproval || …` short-circuit in `processGatewayAllowlist`, so the deny-over-allow guarantee cannot regress even if `requiresExecApproval`'s denylist handling ever changes.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's exec approvals support allowlists but no denylist: there is no way to force human approval (or denial) for specific dangerous commands when an agent runs at `security=full` / `ask=off`, or when a broad allowlist/durable trust would otherwise auto-approve them. #6615 asks for a deny-over-allow screening layer so commands like `git push --force` or `rm -rf` patterns always require an explicit human decision, regardless of permissive settings.

## Fix

- `src/infra/exec-approvals-denylist.ts`: entry normalization, strict validation (`collectExecDenylistErrors`), and `resolveEffectiveExecDenylist` (de-duplicated union across layers — deny anywhere = deny).
- **Both config layers**: `openclaw.json` `tools.exec.denylist` (global + per-agent) **and** `~/.openclaw/exec-approvals.json` (defaults + `*` + agent), wired through both exec hosts (see Update above).
- **Shared pattern language**: denylist patterns reuse the existing allowlist glob compiler via a new `matchesExecGlob` export — no second matcher to keep in sync (`*` → `[^/]*`, `**` → `.*`, `?` → `[^/]`).
- **Deny wins first**: a hit forces approval ahead of `ask=off`, `security=full`, allowlist hits, and durable allow-always trust, on both the gateway exec host and node-host `system.run` (node denial reason `denylist-hit`). Explicit allow-once approval still clears a hit; `security=deny` still wins overall.
- Conservative fallback: unanalyzable command + configured denylist ⇒ approval required, not fail-open. Basename variants and `bash -c "..."` inner payloads are screened.

## Evidence

**Typecheck (repo's real TS-Go checker):** `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` both clean on this branch. (Stock `tsc` throws a bogus TS4058 in `src/secrets/config-io.ts` that tsgo does not — pre-existing on `main`.)

**Focused tests — all green on the exact paths flagged:**
- `src/infra/exec-approvals-denylist.test.ts` — 19 (normalize/dedupe, both-layer union, exact/glob/basename/wrapper matches, conservative fallback, precedence).
- `src/node-host/exec-policy.test.ts` — 19 and `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.test.ts` — 36 (node-host `system.run` enforcement, config-layer union, human-only, `denylist-hit`).
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts` — 54 (gateway standalone denylist gate at `security=full`/`ask=off`).
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/exec-approvals-validators.test.ts` — 8 (protocol/file denylist round-trip).
- `src/config/config.schema-regressions.test.ts` — 39 and `src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts` — 23 (config schema accept/validate + label/help coverage).

> Note: on a host that symlinks `head` to cargo-coreutils, one unrelated pre-existing test (`processGatewayAllowlist > uses a plan-backed enforced command…`) fails on a `/usr/bin/head` vs `/usr/lib/cargo/bin/coreutils/head` path assertion. It is environmental and independent of this PR (our diff to that test file is additive only).

**Real behavior proof** (real decision code path via `node --import tsx`, no test doubles — `git push --force origin main` allowlisted + durable-trusted at `security=full`/`ask=off`, denylist supplied through the openclaw.json config layer exactly as the wired callers do):

```
## BEFORE (control: no denylist configured)
[gateway-host] command="git push --force origin main" security=full ask=off allowlisted=true durable=true -> AUTO-RUN
[node-host]    command="git push --force origin main" -> ALLOWED

## AFTER (denylist configured via openclaw.json tools.exec.denylist)
denylist = [{"pattern":"git push*--force*","reason":"history rewrite"}]
[gateway-host] -> APPROVAL REQUIRED
[node-host]    -> DENIED (denylist-hit)

## AFTER + explicit allow-once approval
[node-host]    -> ALLOWED (approval cleared the hit)
```

## Scope notes

- Contract is now complete across config schema, gateway protocol write schema, gateway host caller, node-host `system.run`, docs/help (`schema.help.ts` + `schema.labels.ts`), tests, and real proof.
- No drive-by refactors.


## Node-host prompt parity (b0164f0fe8a, 2026-07-09)

Review found that the `host=node` `security=full`/`ask=off` fast path invoked `system.run` directly before prepare/approval registration, so a denylist STOP rule hard-denied server-side (`denylist-hit`) instead of raising the documented human allow-once prompt.

Fixed for prompt parity (recommended option):

- The direct fast path is taken only when the caller-visible effective denylist is **known empty**: the `openclaw.json` config layer is empty AND the node approvals-file denylist (fetched via `exec.approvals.node.get`) is known and empty. Fetch failures fail **closed** into the prepare path.
- On the prepare path, the effective denylist (config layer + node approvals-file layer) is evaluated caller-side; a hit forces a registered human approval request even at full/off, mirroring the gateway host: auto-review is excluded (human-only), and `allow-always` is downgraded to one-shot so no durable trust can be minted from a denylist hit.
- Non-matching commands with a configured denylist still auto-run (via the prepare path); setups with no denylist keep the direct fast path.

Focused tests added in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts`: config-layer hit registers an approval request (no direct denial), approvals-file hit registers an approval request, non-matching denylist auto-runs, known-empty denylist keeps the fast path, approvals fetch failure fails closed to prepare. `vitest run src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts src/infra/exec-approvals-denylist.test.ts src/node-host/exec-policy.test.ts --pool=forks` => 4 files, 146 tests passed; tsgo typecheck clean.

Honest proof status: production decision-function proof and the focused node-host approval-registration tests are in; a live gateway+node prompt -> allow-once -> runs-exactly-once capture is being prepared on a dedicated QA host and will be appended when complete.

Known residual (intentional, documented here): a denylist configured ONLY in the node machine's own local `openclaw.json` remains invisible to the gateway-side caller and still hard-denies server-side (fail-closed). The two operator surfaces this PR documents (`tools.exec.denylist` config layer and the exec-approvals file) now both get prompt parity on host=node.

target.title: fix(dreaming): drop heartbeat assistant responses from dream corpus
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The dreaming ingestion pipeline filters heartbeat **user** messages (containing `[OpenClaw heartbeat poll]`) via `sanitizeSessionText`, but the paired **assistant** response was only dropped when it was the exact string `HEARTBEAT_OK`. Local models frequently respond with natural-language acknowledgments (e.g. "Heartbeat received. Main is active.") which pass through the sanitizer unchanged and enter the dream corpus as low-confidence memory snippets.

See issue #103720.

## Why This Change Was Made

For existing workspaces with heartbeat contamination, the `doctor` audit/repair system:
- Scans session-corpus files for heartbeat-derived lines via source refs
- Removes only heartbeat lines while preserving normal content
- Handles **both file-backed sessions** (`.jsonl` paths) and **SQLite-backed sessions** (logical paths without extension) via a fallback to `loadTranscriptEventsSync`
- Avoids clearing session ingestion checkpoints to prevent corpus duplication on re-ingestion
- Falls through to self-ingestion narrative content checks even when heartbeat contamination is found

target.title: fix(exec): memoize duplicate auto-review verdicts
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the exec approval path and understand the authorization boundary changed by this patch.

## What Problem This Solves

Addresses #102249.

The model-backed exec auto-reviewer pays for a fresh reviewer completion whenever the same ask-requiring gateway request is reviewed again. Retry and polling loops can therefore turn N identical reviews into N paid model calls even though the reviewer runs deterministically at temperature 0.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a bounded per-reviewer-instance memo with deliberately narrow reuse semantics:

- cache only completed low-risk `allow-once` decisions for `host=gateway`;
- require a non-empty canonical gateway `resolvedPath` before caching;
- key command, argv, resolved executable, cwd, environment keys, reason, analysis, and agent context;
- never cache node-host requests, `ask`, timeout, unavailable-model, completion-error, or other fallback outcomes;
- cap the memo at 128 entries.

Node-host reuse was explicitly removed after review because its current prepare protocol does not expose a separate canonical resolved-executable field to the reviewer. This avoids crossing node or executable authorization boundaries rather than widening the protocol in a cost-optimization PR.

## User Impact

For N byte-identical gateway requests within one reviewer instance, paid reviewer completions drop from N to 1. Changed resolved executables trigger a fresh completion, and node requests retain the existing per-call review behavior.

target.title: fix: prevent completed Codex hook relays from lingering
target.body:
Closes #106838

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running native Codex hooks could leave completed OpenClaw relay CLI processes alive when CLI setup or a handler retained a referenced Node handle. Repeated parallel hook events could therefore accumulate process trees and memory after their relay work had finished.

## Why This Change Was Made

The hidden `hooks relay` command now uses the existing deferred one-shot shutdown path after its handler returns. The shared wrapper propagates the relay's numeric exit code, lets `runCli` complete normal harness, proxy, memory, and stdin teardown, and drains stdout and stderr before exiting. This does not change the native relay protocol, gateway behavior, configuration, or external timeout handling before a relay handler completes.

## User Impact

Completed native Codex hook relays now terminate even when a referenced Node handle would otherwise keep the CLI alive. This prevents completed relay processes from accumulating across parallel tool batches while preserving Codex-compatible output and exit statuses.

## What Problem This Solves

Release validation used `gh run watch`, which repeatedly consumed REST quota and produced noisy full-job output. Separately, `scripts/pr prepare-*` and `merge-*` silently assumed a `main` base; using them on a release-branch PR rebased the prep branch onto `origin/main` before the operator could stop it.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Monitor the exact Full Release Validation workflow via paginated GraphQL check-suite metadata, matching the 64-bit-safe workflow URL. Polling is bounded, retries transient query failures, and preserves the existing success/failure and evidence-verification contract.
- Fail closed before lock/worktree mutation when prepare or merge commands receive a non-`main` PR.
- Record the concise invocation rules that prevented the observed `rg` and release-branch formatter mistakes.
- Repair exact-head CI regressions exposed by the first hosted run: declare the new helper export, privatize three internal symbols, remove a duplicate SQLite guardrail entry, and assert the current cron process-instance response.
- Repair moving-main merge-ref regressions exposed by the next hosted run: make the new Telegram wait lint-clean and replace a descriptor-number reuse assertion with a direct close-call contract.

target.title: fix(agents): terminate agent run on critical loop detection instead of continuing indefinitely
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Critical loop detection correctly blocks a stuck tool (`deniedReason: "tool-loop"`, `action=block`), but the blocked result was returned as an ordinary tool result. The agent kept issuing provider turns and re-calling the same tool for hours (#106231).

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper Rank-up on the previous abort-helper tip required the **canonical agent-core termination contracts** instead of `abortRun` at the embedded-run boundary (which records synthetic `stopReason: "aborted"` and can cancel sibling tools in mixed batches).

Dual-layer stop:

1. **Per-result** `terminate: true` on critical tool-loop blocked results → `shouldTerminateToolBatch` stops single/all-veto batches.
2. **Post-turn** `shouldStopAfterTurn` in `createAgentSession` → stops **mixed** batches when any finalized result has `deniedReason: "tool-loop"`.

Plugin / approval vetoes stay non-terminating.

## User Impact

- Critical tool loops terminate the agent run instead of burning tokens indefinitely.
- Mixed parallel batches complete non-loop tools, then stop before the next provider turn.
- Non-loop blocks unchanged.
- Terminal outcome follows normal loop completion (not a synthetic aborted assistant message from embedded `abortRun`).

## Evidence

**Head SHA:** `59977a726886274d04a036be59c7392972d67db9` (rebuilt from current `main`; replaces prior `critical-tool-loop-abort` approach)

**Patch quality:** platinum-shaped — 6 files, +232/−1 net, single owner boundary, no speculative exports, clean compare vs main.

| Rank-up | Status |
|---|---|
| Replace embedded abort with terminate + post-turn contracts | done |
| Cover single-tool + mixed-batch | done (`agent-loop.test.ts`, `blocked-result.test.ts`) |
| e2e asserts `terminate: true` on tool-loop blocks | done |
| Real-runtime transcript (no next provider turn; no unintended aborted entry) | **pending L3** — need live agent credentials/run |

### Commands (green locally)

```text
$ node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check <touched 6 files>
All matched files use the correct format.

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.test.ts -t "critical|shouldStopAfterTurn|mixed batch"
✓ mixed batch shouldStopAfterTurn
✓ Agent.prompt single critical terminate
Tests  2 passed | 25 skipped

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.blocked-result.test.ts
Test Files  2 shards passed (4 + 27)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.e2e.test.ts -t "loop detection"
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  38 passed | 45 skipped
```

### Before / after (contract)

| Case | BEFORE | AFTER |
|---|---|---|
| Critical tool-loop block (single tool) | result returned; model continues | `terminate: true` → batch terminates; no next provider turn |
| Critical tool-loop in mixed batch | continue if not every result terminates | `shouldStopAfterTurn` stops after turn |
| Other blocked reasons | unchanged | unchanged (no `terminate`) |

Fixes #106231

target.title: fix(tools-manager): use BigInt for lossless Content-Length comparison
target.body:
## Summary
Replace `Number()` + `isSafeInteger` with `BigInt()` for lossless Content-Length comparison in `downloadFile`.

## What Problem This Solves
`Number()` can lose precision when parsing large integer strings (≥16 digits). The existing `CONTENT_LENGTH_RE` regex `/^\d+$/` matches arbitrarily long digit strings with no upper bound, but `Number("9007199254740993")` returns `9007199254740992` — a different value.

Although `isSafeInteger` catches most precision-loss cases (any value that rounds above `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`), relying on `Number()` for integer comparison is fragile. A Content-Length string of 20+ digits like `"99999999999999999999"` becomes `100000000000000000000` through `Number()` — completely wrong.

In practice `MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES` is 100 MB (~10⁸), so any oversized Content-Length is caught by the numeric comparison long before precision becomes an issue. This is a **correctness hardening** — using the right tool (`BigInt`) for integer comparison so the code is obviously correct at all scales.

**Code evidence**: in `src/agents/utils/tools-manager.ts:187-188`, the current code parses Content-Length through `Number()` which is not guaranteed lossless for arbitrary-length digit strings.

## Root Cause
The code was written using `Number()` for integer parsing, which is lossy for values beyond 2⁵³ − 1 (`Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` = 9,007,199,254,740,991). The `isSafeInteger` guard partially mitigates this but:
1. It rejects values for the wrong reason (precision loss vs size cap)
2. The error message says "exceeds byte limit" when actually the value can't be accurately parsed
3. It relies on an indirect property (safe integer vs range check) rather than comparing the value directly

## Why This Fix
**Chosen approach**: `BigInt(contentLength) > BigInt(maxBytes)` — one-line replacement.

- **Correct**: `BigInt` preserves the exact integer from any digit string
- **Simpler**: replaces two conditions (`!isSafeInteger || > maxBytes`) with one (`> maxBytes`)
- **Proven**: `BigInt` is already used elsewhere in the codebase (`src/infra/kysely-sync.ts` etc.)
- **Minimal**: 2 lines removed, 1 line added

Alternatives considered:
- String length pre-check: avoids the problem but is ad-hoc
- `BigInt` + fallback: unnecessary — `BigInt` is well-supported in Node 22

## User Impact
No user-visible change. The existing behavior was already correct for all practical Content-Length values (≤ a few GB). This fix hardens the code against theoretically large Content-Length headers and makes the intent clearer.

## Evidence
- **Before (Number() approach)**: `Number("9007199254740993")` → `9007199254740992` (precision LOST). `Number("99999999999999999999")` → `100000000000000000000` (massively wrong). ❌ FAIL
- **After (BigInt() approach)**: `BigInt("9007199254740993")` → `9007199254740993n` (exact). `BigInt("99999999999999999999")` → `99999999999999999999n` (exact). ✓ PASS

## Real Behavior Proof

### Before (Number() approach — precision loss)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
============================================================
Content-Length precision loss demonstration
============================================================
Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER = 9007199254740991

--- Case 1: Large Content-Length (above MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) ---
Content-Length header: "9007199254740993"
Number("9007199254740993") = 9007199254740992
Actual BigInt value : 9007199254740993
Precision preserved?  : NO — LOST!

Old code (Number + isSafeInteger):
  declaredBytes = Number("9007199254740993") = 9007199254740992
  isSafeInteger(9007199254740992) = false
  => REJECT (declaredBytes=9007199254740992, reason="exceeds cap or not safe integer")

--- Case 3: 20-digit Content-Length ---
Number("99999999999999999999") = 100000000000000000000
Number result accurate?  NO — massively wrong!

FAIL: Number() lost precision on Content-Length '9007199254740993'
FAIL: Number() returned wrong value for 20-digit Content-Length
```

### After (BigInt() comparison — exact)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
--- Case 1: Large Content-Length (above MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) ---
New code (BigInt comparison):
  BigInt("9007199254740993") = 9007199254740993n
  9007199254740993n > 10n = true
  => REJECT (reason="exceeds cap")

--- Case 2: Normal Content-Length (within safe range) ---
Old: ACCEPT  |  New: ACCEPT

PASS: BigInt() preserves exact value: 9007199254740993n
```

## Tests and Validation
- `pnpm check` passed
- `vitest run src/agents/utils/tools-manager.test.ts` — 18 tests passed (2 new: large Content-Length rejection)
- Added regression test: "rejects downloads with large Content-Length that would lose precision with Number()"

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Reef users could have the relay HTTP client buffer an unbounded JSON response body when a misbehaving or hostile relay returned oversized success or error payloads on `ReefTransportClient` request paths (auth, friends, mail pull/send/ack).

Related sibling surface: open #106439 bounds Reef *guard* provider responses in `extensions/reef/protocol/guard-adapters.ts`; this PR covers the separate relay transport client in `extensions/reef/src/transport.ts`, which still used unbounded `response.json()`.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ReefTransportClient.request` now reads JSON through the shared `readProviderJsonResponse` helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-http`:

- success bodies capped at 16 MiB (`reef.relay`)
- error bodies capped at 64 KiB (`reef.relay.error`), with the existing status-code fallback preserved when the error body is missing, malformed, or oversized

Oversized streams are cancelled before the remainder is buffered. Non-goal: changing guard adapters (owned by #106439) or adding new config.

## User Impact

Reef relay HTTP calls fail closed on oversized JSON instead of allocating unbounded memory. Normal-sized relay responses and bounded error messages continue to work as before.

## Evidence

Head: `7d4ab0a3461a71021bd0d0ba53d5aade8573206f`

**Head:** `f8d35557ae69c3e457b601cbe2bc535049689032`

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators using Codex app-server over `websocket`/`unix` transport would hang forever on `initialize`/RPC when a peer accepted TCP but never completed the WebSocket upgrade. ## Why This Change Was Made

- Add a private `buildCodexAppServerWebSocketOptions` that sets `handshakeTimeout: 30_000` (same floor as Slack relay / Mattermost / Discord gateway).
- Both TCP and Unix upgrade paths consume that builder.
- Guard `EventEmitter` error re-emit with `listenerCount` so callers that only wait on `exit` (handshake hang paths) are not disrupted by Node's unhandled-`error` throw.
- Regressions observe production wiring in source (knip-safe) and prove stalled-handshake exit + `initialize` failure with a short test-only hang floor.

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** A Codex app-server endpoint that accepted TCP without completing the websocket handshake could pin `initialize`/RPC forever on that attempt.

**After:** Handshake waits fail closed after 30s (`Opening handshake has timed out` → transport `exit` / client error), so the run can stop or recover instead of hanging.

## Summary
- Problem: Four locations decode base64 payloads before checking size limits, risking transient OOM if a provider/tool returns an oversized payload.
- Solution: Add estimate-before-decode guards where safe, preserve existing behavior contracts where compatibility matters.
- What changed:
  - `src/agents/cli-runner/helpers.ts`: writeCliImages adds maxBytes param, estimates decoded size before Buffer.from
  - `src/image-generation/image-assets.ts`: Estimates decoded size before canonicalization to avoid transient string allocation; propagates maxBytes through `generatedImageAssetFromBase64`, `generatedImageAssetFromOpenAiCompatibleEntry`, and `parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse`
  - `src/image-generation/openai-compatible-image-provider.ts`: Wires `resolveGeneratedMediaMaxBytes(req.cfg, "image")` into `parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse`
  - `extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.ts`: Wires `resolveGeneratedImageMaxBytes` into OpenAI image generation path
  - `extensions/google/image-generation-provider.ts`: Wires `resolveGeneratedImageMaxBytes` into Google image generation path
  - `extensions/openrouter/image-generation-provider.ts`: Wires `resolveGeneratedImageMaxBytes` into OpenRouter image extraction path
- What did NOT change: `resizeImage` still attempts resize before rejecting (maxBytes is an output target, not an input ceiling); `generatedMusicAssetFromBase64` still returns guaranteed result for SDK compatibility.

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

target.title: Redact exec tool result payloads
target.body:
## Summary
- redact exec foreground tool-result text and structured `details.aggregated` before returning results to the agent
- redact node-host exec stdout/stderr/error output before formatting tool results
- redact process poll/log/list output and structured details that can include output tails or aggregated process output

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** Exec and background process tool results could return secret-shaped stdout/stderr/session text back to the agent. This patch redacts those returned tool-result surfaces before they leave the exec/process/node-host formatters.

**Real environment tested:** Real local OpenClaw checkout on branch `fix/exec-tool-result-redaction` at `da701a0bbf6c`, using an isolated temporary `OPENCLAW_HOME`. The proof used an obvious fake canary value, not a real credential.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Ran a local runtime proof that exercised `createExecTool` and `createProcessTool` with a fake `REDACTION_CANARY_SECRET` value, then inspected the returned tool-result `content[0].text` and structured `details.aggregated` values for foreground exec, process poll, process log, and process list tail/details surfaces.

**Evidence after fix:** Copied live output from the local runtime proof:

```json
{
  "foregroundExec": {
    "status": "completed",
    "text": "REDACTION_CANARY_SECRET=clawsw…7890",
    "detailsAggregated": "REDACTION_CANARY_SECRET=clawsw…7890",
    "rawCanaryValuePresent": false,
    "redactedMarkerPresent": true
  },
  "processPoll": {
    "status": "completed",
    "text": "REDACTION_CANARY_SECRET=clawsw…7890\n\n\nProcess exited with code 0.",
    "detailsAggregated": "REDACTION_CANARY_SECRET=clawsw…7890\n",
    "rawCanaryValuePresent": false,
    "redactedMarkerPresent": true
  },
  "processLog": {
    "status": "completed",
    "text": "REDACTION_CANARY_SECRET=clawsw…7890",
    "detailsAggregated": "",
    "rawCanaryValuePresent": false,
    "redactedMarkerPresent": true
  },
  "processList": {
    "status": "completed",
    "textTail": "REDACTION_CANARY_SECRET=clawsw…7890",
    "rawCanaryValuePresent": false,
    "redactedMarkerPresent": true
  }
}
```

Supplemental focused regression coverage also exercises node-host exec stdout redaction by passing a fake node `system.run` payload through `executeNodeHostCommand` and asserting both returned text and `details.aggregated` redact the raw canary.

**Observed result after fix:** The raw fake canary value was absent from returned foreground exec, process poll, process log, and process list output. Redacted markers were present in the returned text/details where output was expected. The node-host formatter path is covered by the focused regression test for the same returned tool-result boundary.

**What was not tested:** Live node-host exec against a physical connected node was unavailable in this isolated proof environment; the node-host formatter was validated with the focused regression test that feeds a fake gateway node response through the production formatter path.

## Tests
- `corepack pnpm exec oxfmt --write --threads=1 src/agents/bash-tools.exec.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node-phases.ts src/agents/bash-tools.process.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-foreground-failures.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.process.poll-timeout.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`
- `corepack pnpm tsgo:core`
- `corepack pnpm tsgo:core:test`
- `corepack pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-foreground-failures.test.ts -t 'redacts secret-shaped stdout'`
- `corepack pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/bash-tools.process.poll-timeout.test.ts -t 'redacts secret-shaped output'`
- `corepack pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts -t 'redacts secret-shaped node stdout'`

Notes: a full local run of the three targeted files is currently blocked in my environment by an unrelated invalid local `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` model alias (`openai-codex/gpt-5.3-codex`) during the pre-existing foreground timeout test. The new redaction regression tests pass individually under the agents-core Vitest config.

Fixes #71211



## Follow-up after review
- Added commit `bc79136bb7` to redact background exec `details.tail` before returning running-session tool results.
- Added regression coverage for background exec `details.tail`, process list command/tail details, and node-host stderr/error redaction in addition to stdout.

Additional local verification after follow-up:
- `corepack pnpm tsgo:core`
- `corepack pnpm tsgo:core:test`
- `corepack pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-foreground-failures.test.ts -t 'redacts secret-shaped'`
- `corepack pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/bash-tools.process.poll-timeout.test.ts -t 'redacts secret-shaped'`
- `corepack pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts -t 'redacts secret-shaped node'`
- `git diff --check`

Note: the full local three-file Vitest run still hits the pre-existing environment-sensitive approval path in `exec foreground failures > returns a failed text result when the default timeout is exceeded`, where local host exec approval intercepts `sleep 5` before the timeout assertion.

## Review feedback update - 2026-05-21
- Addressed ClawSweeper P1 by removing the JSON embedded-fallback behavior change from this PR; `openclaw agent --json` fallback behavior is back to the existing contract.
- Addressed ClawSweeper P2 by replacing the live-update process timing test with deterministic `runExecProcess` regression coverage, so the previous single-line skip branches are gone.
- Final head verified: `8793847f206cca93c49abe33e4f49b9b55a0c4dc`.

Additional verification on final head:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.exec-foreground-failures.test.ts -t 'redacts secret-shaped'`\n- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.test.ts -t 'redacts secret-shaped stdout in update text and details tail'`\n- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts -t 'JSON'`\n- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.process.poll-timeout.test.ts -t 'redacts secret-shaped'`\n- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts -t 'redacts secret-shaped node'`\n- `pnpm exec oxlint src/agents/bash-tools.exec-foreground-failures.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.test.ts src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts src/cli/program/register.agent.ts src/cli/program/register.agent.test.ts`\n- `git diff --check && git diff --cached --check`\n\nChanged-file gate note: `node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs run --shell -- "pnpm check:changed"` did not reach pnpm because local `crabbox` failed its binary sanity check. Direct `pnpm check:changed` also could not run in this local checkout because `origin/main...HEAD` has no merge base on the grafted/shallow branch. The focused tests, lint, and diff checks above passed on the final head.

## Process control redaction update - 2026-05-21
- Addressed ClawSweeper P1 by redacting command-derived process result names for running-session controls (`write`, `submit`, `paste`) plus `kill`, `remove`, `poll`, `log`, `list`, and `send-keys`.
- Added fake-secret regression coverage for `process write` and `process send-keys` command-derived `details.name` values.
- Final head verified locally: `24ac21f4280e9e403722c271d12fda0a4c68535d4`.

Additional verification on final head:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.process.poll-timeout.test.ts -t 'redacts secret-shaped'`\n- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.process-send-keys.test.ts -t 'redacts secret-shaped'`\n- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.exec-foreground-failures.test.ts -t 'redacts secret-shaped'`\n- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.test.ts -t 'redacts secret-shaped stdout in update text and details tail'`\n- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts -t 'redacts secret-shaped node'`\n- `pnpm exec oxlint src/agents/bash-tools.process.ts src/agents/bash-tools.process-send-keys.ts src/agents/bash-tools.process.poll-timeout.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.process-send-keys.test.ts`\n- `git diff --check && git diff --cached --check`

target.title: fix(node-pairing): require operator.admin to approve fs.listDir nodes (#105936)
target.body:
Closes #105936


## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators with only `operator.pairing` and `operator.write` scopes (without `operator.admin`) could approve a node surface that declares `fs.listDir`, even though invoking `fs.listDir` via `node.invoke` already correctly requires `operator.admin`. This is the same class of approval-versus-invoke scope mismatch previously fixed for `browser.proxy` in #104491.

## Why This Change Was Made

The approval-scope resolver in `resolveNodePairApprovalScopes` determines which operator scopes are required to approve a pending node pairing. It maintains an admin-level command list (`ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS`) that dictates which declared commands demand `operator.admin` at approval time. `fs.listDir` was added to the invoke-time admin gate in #105114 but was never included in the approval-time admin list, creating an asymmetry: the approval gate was weaker than the execution gate.

This change adds `NODE_FS_LIST_DIR_COMMAND` to `ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS`, making the approval-time scope requirement match the existing invoke-time requirement. The approach is identical to the `browser.proxy` fix in #104491.

## User Impact

Operators with `operator.pairing` and `operator.write` can no longer approve a node pairing that declares `fs.listDir`. Such approvals now require `operator.admin`, consistent with the existing invoke-time authorization. Existing approved pairings are unaffected.

## Evidence

- **Unit test**: `resolveNodePairApprovalScopes(["fs.listDir"])` now returns `["operator.pairing", "operator.admin"]`

```
✓ |unit-fast| src/infra/node-pairing-authz.test.ts (6 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  6 passed (6)
```

- **Integration test**: Full `node.pair.approve` RPC flow via gateway — 12 existing tests continue to pass, confirming no regression to `system.run`, `browser.proxy`, or non-admin command approval paths.

```
✓ |gateway-server| src/gateway/server.node-pairing-authz.test.ts (12 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  12 passed (12)
```

- **Type check**: `tsgo:core` passes without errors.

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: an `operator.write` (non-admin) operator can approve a node advertising the `fs.listDir` capability, whereas invoking `fs.listDir` requires `operator.admin`; the fix makes approval require `operator.admin` too.

Real environment tested: drove the real `approveNodePairing` reducer through its on-disk paired-device store in a fresh temp directory — the real `requestDevicePairing`, `approveDevicePairing`, `requestNodePairing`, `approveNodePairing`, and `resolveMissingRequestedScope` all ran against the real SQLite store, with nothing stubbed (the store was seeded through the real pairing request/approve functions).

Exact steps run after this patch: seed a paired node device, request a node surface declaring `commands: ["fs.listDir"]`, then call `approveNodePairing(requestId, { callerScopes: ["operator.pairing", "operator.write"] }, baseDir)` and record the returned outcome.

Evidence after fix:

```
caller scopes: [operator.pairing, operator.write]
surface commands: [fs.listDir]
approveNodePairing -> FORBIDDEN missingScope=operator.admin

caller scopes: [operator.pairing, operator.admin]
surface commands: [fs.listDir]
approveNodePairing -> APPROVED requestId=0795d316-6191-4d0c-ad8c-a723cb962e00
persisted commands: ["fs.listDir"]
```

## Reviewer Notes

Codex's review notes that the two admin-command classifications
(`ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS` and `ADMIN_ONLY_NODE_INVOKE_COMMANDS`) are
independently maintained, which has now caused two authorization mismatches
(#104491 for `browser.proxy`, this PR for `fs.listDir`).

This concern is well understood. However, the two lists are not identical by
design: `ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS` includes `system.run.*` (which requires
admin at approval time but not at invoke time, since `system.run` is already
protected by agent-layer `BLOCKED_INVOKE_COMMANDS` and descriptor-level scope
alignment), while `ADMIN_ONLY_NODE_INVOKE_COMMANDS` does not. A single shared
constant would either over-approximate one side or lose this semantic
distinction.

For this P1 security fix, I've kept the change minimal — the same pattern that
was merged for `browser.proxy` in #104491. Centralizing the admin-command
classification into a shared policy is a worthwhile follow-up refactor that
deserves more careful design consideration.

target.title: fix(ai): safely format circular rejections in stream catch paths
target.body:
Closes #106570
Related: #106568

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where provider stream failure handling could throw a second exception when formatting a non-Error rejection that contains circular references. That second throw prevented a clean terminal error event and stream end on OpenAI Completions (and the sibling Google shared stream path), so agent runs could hang or fail without a structured provider error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Introduces a shared `formatUnknownError` helper that prefers `Error.message`, safely JSON-stringifies ordinary values, falls back to `String(error)` when `JSON.stringify` throws, and returns the constant `"Unknown error"` if `String()` itself throws (null-prototype or hostile conversion hooks). The OpenAI Completions, Google shared, and Anthropic stream catch paths use it so terminal stream termination cannot be broken by circular or hostile rejection payloads. OpenAI Responses/Azure already guarded stringify; this keeps the unsafe catch sites consistent without new config or fallback policy.

Fix quality: compatibility — no API/config shape change, same errorMessage field; performance — O(1) catch-path only; usability — still delivers a terminal error message; security — no secret logging or trust-boundary changes.

## User Impact

When a provider transport rejects with an unusual non-Error object (including circular structures or values whose String conversion throws), the agent stream fails closed with a normal error stop reason and message instead of throwing inside the recovery path.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Node v24.17.0)

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/utils/format-unknown-error.test.ts
# 4 passed (Error.message, JSON path, circular String fallback, non-throwing final literal)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.test.ts \
  packages/ai/src/providers/google-shared.test.ts \
  -t "circular"
# 2 passed (OpenAI #106570 + Google #106568 lifecycle: stopReason=error + non-empty errorMessage)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.test.ts -t "circular" --reporter=verbose
# ✓ emits a terminal error for circular non-Error rejections without rethrowing (#106570)

pnpm exec oxfmt --check packages/ai/src/utils/format-unknown-error.ts \
  packages/ai/src/utils/format-unknown-error.test.ts  # pass
git diff --check  # pass
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Stream catch paths must emit a terminal error event when the transport rejects with a circular non-Error value (or a value whose String conversion throws), without a second exception in the recovery path.
- Environment: local macOS openclaw checkout; focused Vitest via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`; Node v24.17.0 runtime transcript for the formatter + stream-shaped terminal events. No live provider credentials required (SDK circular non-Error shapes are not guaranteed from supported providers; proof exercises the catch-path contract the providers call).
- Current-main contrast: On main, `error instanceof Error ? error.message : JSON.stringify(error)` throws `TypeError: Converting circular structure to JSON` for self-referential objects, so the catch path never reaches `stream.push({ type: "error" })` / `stream.end()`. Reproduced with: `const c={k:1}; c.self=c; JSON.stringify(c)` → throws.
- Exact steps after this patch:
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/utils/format-unknown-error.test.ts`
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.test.ts -t "circular"`
  3. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/google-shared.test.ts -t "circular"`
  4. Runtime transcript (formatter + stream-shaped terminal emission; redacted, no secrets):
```text
=== formatUnknownError runtime proof (redacted) ===
host: darwin v24.17.0
before: JSON.stringify(circular) throws: true
format(circular): threw=false value="[object Object]"
format(null-proto-circular): threw=false value="Unknown error"
format(hostile-circular): threw=false value="Unknown error"
format(Error): threw=false value="upstream boom"
format(plain-object): threw=false value="{\"code\":\"ECONNRESET\"}"

=== stream catch-path terminal emission (synthetic runtime, OpenAI Completions shape) ===
case=circular-non-Error
  output.stopReason= error
  output.errorMessage= [object Object]
  events= [{"type":"error","reason":"error","errorMessage":"[object Object]"},{"type":"end"}]
  stream_closed= true
case=null-proto-circular
  output.stopReason= error
  output.errorMessage= Unknown error
  events= [{"type":"error","reason":"error","errorMessage":"Unknown error"},{"type":"end"}]
  stream_closed= true
case=hostile-circular
  output.stopReason= error
  output.errorMessage= Unknown error
  events= [{"type":"error","reason":"error","errorMessage":"Unknown error"},{"type":"end"}]
  stream_closed= true
proof_ok=true
```
- Evidence after fix: Focused OpenAI/Google lifecycle cases pass with `stopReason === "error"` and a non-empty `errorMessage`. Helper never throws: circular → `[object Object]`; null-prototype/hostile circular → `"Unknown error"`. Runtime events show `{type:"error"}` then stream end for each case.
- Control check: Ordinary Error rejections still use `error.message`; ordinary plain objects still JSON-stringify; only circular non-Errors take the String fallback; only values that break both JSON and String take the constant literal.
- Observed result after fix: Circular and hostile non-Error rejections produce a terminal stream error instead of a secondary serialization/conversion crash.
- What was not tested: Live OpenAI/Google network failures that happen to reject with circular non-Error SDK payloads; Anthropic live path (same helper wired for sibling invariant only).

---

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text

- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Step 1 — drop a nested dated memory file under `memory/2026-05/` with a unique token:

```
cat > ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku/memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md <<'EOF'
Recursive memory search proof.
Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
EOF
```

Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:


target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
